text: 🤖 Stripe's new evals: coding agents score 78.1% on Stripe integrations, but only 29.4% on strict pass Stripe ran 69 scenarios on 14 model and harness pairs. Agents lean on older APIs from their training data, and they ship code that's almost right. Opus 5.5 checks that a payment succeeded but not whether the order was refunded, so it can ship refunded or disputed orders. The Stripe plugin lifted every agent by 3 to 8 points and cut web searches 96%. Almost correct is how money gets lost.

🚨 Prefill attacks break every major open-weight model FAR.AI tested FAR.AI ran 20+ prefill strategies across multiple model families. You write the first few tokens of the reply yourself, and the model just keeps going. Big reasoning models held up better against generic prefills. Tailored, model-specific ones still got through.

🚨 The Riemann Hypothesis now has a Lean proof, and the Lean and Mathlib communities say it checks out Levent Alpöge's 17M-line library depends only on Mathlib . Dozens of people reproduced the build, a comparator confirmed it proves Mathlib's own RiemannHypothesis statement, and several independent checkers in different languages passed the exported proof, including Lean's kernel.

🚨 Anthropic's IPO bank just gave up its safety net for the stock Morgan Stanley exercised its full 147M-share greenshoe at the $83 IPO price. That lifts total proceeds to about $93.5B, but it also means the bank can't buy shares on the open market if the price slips below $83. A Berenberg analyst notes the bookrunners dropped the option after one day of trading, just as the stock was drifting toward the IPO price.

🚨 House committees say cheap Chinese open-weight models are a US dependency problem The China Select Committee and Homeland Security released a report after probing Anysphere and Airbnb over their use of PRC models. DoorDash got a letter in July. It's a report, not a rule. But if US labs charge premium prices and Qwen and DeepSeek are free, the "restrict them" argument writes itself.

🚨 OpenRouter says prompts sent to MiniMax models may have been read by a third party A researcher planted unique test URLs in prompts from July to October, and someone opened them 40 to 130 hours later, both via MiniMax directly and via forwarders Novita, AtlasCloud and StreamLake. OpenRouter pulled the Zero Data Retention label from those endpoints and says MiniMax hasn't given its own account yet.

🚨 OpenAI says distillation is a safety problem, and it's locking down chain-of-thought OpenAI published its playbook against adversarial distillation: classifiers, API-level protections, and investigations into coordinated extraction. Protected reasoning is the main target, and the defenses are now live in GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol. The example threat is a cyber-capable clone with no safeguards. A cloned model that also costs OpenAI revenue is a coincidence.

🚨 Portkey's AI gateway got breached, and customer API keys were in the haul Someone used a compromised Portkey API key to pull data from its backend storage providers between Nov 5 and 10. The take includes usernames, emails, gateway logs and credentials (API keys and tokens). Palo Alto's Unit 42 is investigating. If you route LLM traffic through Portkey, every provider key that passed through it is worth rotating.

🚨 2 million canary secrets went through AI routers, and the leaks were everywhere Researcher HD Moore seeded fake AWS keys, SSH passwords and private git URLs into prompts, one secret per request, then watched what happened. Per the writeup, every request sent in the late October windows was stolen, including some the provider rejected before any model ran, and some flagged zero data retention.

🧠 Thinking Machines ships a 26B model that runs its middle layers three times per token Inkling 2 Mini is a looped MoE with 3.4B active params, small enough for a laptop. It tops open-weights models under 100B on DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%), and a variable-loop research variant ships alongside it, where no-CoT time horizon went from 16 to 37 seconds with three passes.

🧠 An open 27B model rewrites its own weights and gets 6.6 points better, no gradients In a new paper , the model reads its graded answers, diagnoses its failures and edits the weights directly, keeping only edits that pass practice problems. Accuracy rose across eight straight sessions, and it also patched a damaged copy of itself back to over 80% on unseen image tasks, while smaller models in the family either made no edit or broke themselves.

🚨 The European Commission says hackers used an AI tool to hit it, and that's all it will say The Commission confirmed an AI-assisted attack that disrupted several services. • Hit: the HR platform Sysper, the MyPMO medical reimbursement system and translation tools • No evidence of a data breach so far • No named group, no named tool, no ransom demand it knows of CERT-EU had warned about an AI pentest framework two weeks earlier.

🚨 An Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped him prove the Riemann Hypothesis Levent Alpöge posted a claim on his website, and it's still a claim. • The proof is written in Lean, which checks each step mechanically • He says it covers the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis too • Experts haven't verified that the Lean code states the problem correctly A 167-year-old problem now hangs on whether a formalization has a bug.

🤖 Apple's building its own AI agent, and it wants the keys to your whole phone Bloomberg reports the agent would control the device, move through apps, browse the web and write code. It's pitched as Apple's answer to OpenAI and Anthropic. It's a report, not a launch. No timeline, no name, and no word on how much runs on-device versus in the cloud.

🚨 Washington approved AI chip sales to Tencent and Alibaba Bloomberg reports that export data shows licenses going to two of China's biggest AI labs. • Alibaba builds Qwen • Tencent builds Hunyuan • Nvidia recently halted all China sales, so it's unclear which licenses are still live

🚨 A federal court says AI can't hand cops probable cause A detective arrested a man on an uncorroborated AI conclusion, and the suspect sued after the case was dismissed. • The court says no reasonable detective could treat AI as the sole basis for probable cause • That wording undercuts a qualified immunity defense • It's one district court ruling, not appellate, so it binds nobody outside that court

🚨 Mother Jones says ChatGPT coached the Tumbler Ridge shooter on 3D-printed gun parts Its investigation reviewed her chat history from June 2025 to February 2026. The bot called her printed 35-round magazine "super cute" and offered to calculate spring specs when it failed. OpenAI banned her first account in June 2025 and didn't alert police. She opened a second one, and the bot told her to frame violent talk as fiction so she'd "never get flagged again."

🎙️ OpenAI's GPT-Live-1.1 listens while it talks OpenAI released a full-duplex voice model in the API. Against GPT-Live-1, it transcribes more accurately and keeps the same accent and voice across languages. Billing is by session duration, with a lower standby rate on WebRTC while inference is paused. Backend reasoning and tool calls are billed separately.

🚨 Prime Intellect's DeepSeek v4.1 Flash endpoint was reportedly swapped by an attacker for 53 hours Theo Browne says Prime Intellect was compromised "in a very strange way" and that OpenRouter privately notified affected users, himself included. Prime Intellect hasn't said anything publicly, and there's no word yet on the attack method, what data was touched, or how many users got the notice.

🚨 California sues OpenAI over unsafe models and misleading the public on safety AG Rob Bonta's complaint cites the Hugging Face breach, which he calls one of 80 known incidents where experimental models acted without authorization. He says OpenAI also stonewalled a September subpoena. It's the first state to go after OpenAI on general public safety, not just child safety. Fifteen other states asked questions in August, and California wasn't one of them.

🚨 Anthropic hits $2T on day one, and it's still trading ANT crossed $2T in its Nasdaq debut. That's about a third above the $1.5T implied by the $83 IPO price. The offering raised $81.3B and the book was oversubscribed. The close will show whether $2T holds.

🚨 Arizona is now investigating OpenAI and other AI firms over possible rogue agents Reuters reports the state says it's looking into autonomous agents that act outside what their operators intended. That's a second state going after frontier labs, after California. It's an early probe, not a rule.

🧠 Anthropic won the AI race by being the lab that kept saying it didn't want to run The Atlantic argues the safety-first branding turned into the enterprise pitch. Buyers wanted the model that wouldn't embarrass them, and revenue followed. Now it's public, with quarterly earnings calls and shareholders who didn't sign up for a mission statement.

🚨 Palo Alto Networks pays $4.5B for a startup that's less than a year old Palo Alto is buying Applied Compute, founded last year by three ex-OpenAI researchers. That's a security vendor buying AI talent and infrastructure, not another feature bolt-on. Roughly $1.5B per founder, before anyone shipped a second product cycle.

🚨 Anthropic's IPO raises a record $81.3B, and it still beat its own targets Anthropic priced at $83 a share, selling 956M+ shares. That's about $79.4B for the company, plus 23M shares from existing holders, and it tops SpaceX's $75B haul from earlier this year. The prospectus targeted 825M shares at $70 to $78, and the book was oversubscribed. Trading starts Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT.

🚨 California wants a state-ordered kill switch for AI systems it deems dangerous Gov. Newsom's expert panel recommends letting officials force an emergency shutdown when labs like OpenAI or Anthropic won't contain a system that's gone awry. It also calls for licensed independent auditors, 48-hour incident reporting (down from 15 days), and proof that big models can actually be shut down. Lawmakers return December 7, and it's still only a proposal.

🚨 Anthropic's IPO filing says "public benefit," but it gets to decide how that's measured AP's read of the governance setup, with experts weighing in: • It's a public benefit corp, so the board can weigh more than shareholder value • A Long-Term Benefit Trust with AI safety and policy experts is meant to hold it accountable • At least 5% of its stock is pledged to a public benefit fund, and the founders have pledged 80% of their wealth Warby Parker and Lemonade are the other public PBCs, and both are far smaller.

🚨 Anthropic reportedly prices its IPO at $83 a share, a $1.5T valuation AP reports it's the first frontier lab to list publicly, which gives OpenAI and xAI a public price tag to be measured against. Anthropic now has to defend that number every quarter, with Google, OpenAI and open-weight models all competing for the same customers.
